cadence_conflict: Handoff reports unseen later30fps-animation owner instruction; scope unresolved before motion. Do not infer cadence from file fps.

checks.requirement: Build around a bizarre scientific “what if” with understandable stakes.
Open with a compelling mystery or contradiction rather than a textbook definition.
Make the opening image and narration immediately reinforce each other.
Deliver useful information early, then deepen the question.
Develop an escalating chain of consequences instead of listing disconnected facts.
Use visual metaphors, comparisons and changes of scale to explain difficult concepts.
Resolve the opening question with a satisfying payoff.
Clearly distinguish the impossible premise, established science and uncertain extrapolation.
Introduce a meaningful visible change every 1.5–2 seconds throughout the explanatory sequence.
Include substantial object animation—not merely photographs entering and then sitting still.
Use movement within compositions: separation, assembly, replacement, transformation, tracking and progressive reveals.
Use purposeful camera pans, close-ups, pullbacks and changes of viewpoint.
Build obvious parallax through independently moving foreground, subject and background layers.
Connect scenes through recognizable objects, directions or ideas.
Give each action an intentional start, acceleration, arrival and reading hold.
Preserve enough reading time for essential text and scientific relationships.
Fully remove departing elements; prevent accidental overlaps and clipped labels.
Evaluate scene and camera animation at 12 distinct states per second.
Export at 1080 × 1920, 30fps, scheduling those states by time.
Keep narration, music and SFX continuous and synchronized.
Judge the stepped motion in playback; do not assume that lowering the frame rate automatically creates appealing animation.
Preserve the exact established ending as the branding exception.
Lead with photographic imagery rather than generic vector icons.
Use high-resolution cutouts with carefully prepared edges and sufficient resolution for close-ups.
Use paper borders, textured labels and collage treatments where they strengthen the composition.
Arrange images to demonstrate relationships and consequences, beyond stacking them on paper.
Create depth through scale, cropping, overlap and independently animated layers.
Use printed diagrams and annotations to support explanations when photographs cannot show the mechanism.
Keep illustrative constructions distinguishable from documentary evidence.
Keep bold Playfair Display headlines and readable Manrope captions.
Animate selected keywords independently from the captions.
Make keywords interact with objects through placement, masking, movement or transformation.
Use bright, deliberate highlights for important distinctions.
Keep captions readable without competing with the main visual.
Add no blurred text duplicates, shadow-like backdrops, halos or glows behind text or graphics.
Include visible paper/material texture and controlled photocopy or film grain.
Use the Cold Metal balance as the benchmark; avoid obscuring photographs with excessive overlays.
Apply restrained chromatic aberration where appropriate.
Use source-image focus changes, compound blur and transition blur to direct attention.
Apply mechanical jitter, brightness variation, edge boil and ink bleed selectively according to the material.
Keep text crisp and the explanatory details legible through the finishing stack.
Write conversationally, with natural emphasis, pauses and changes in delivery.
Retain the approved Bernard voice.
Give meaningful movements synchronized, audible sound cues.
Use paper rustles/card flicks for physical layers, mechanical clicks for text or measurements, and lens/air sounds for camera actions.
Use restrained low-frequency accents for major reveals.
Reuse our existing SFX library first.
Shape the background music around discoveries, tension and resolution.
Prevent overlapping cues from becoming messy or masking narration.
Preserve every spoken word, including the final word and its natural tail.
Deliver the entire episode, not a short excerpt standing in for it.
Review the opening, middle, payoff, transitions and ending in the encoded video.
Check the 1.5–2-second changes against the actual timeline.
Verify that motion develops the explanation rather than providing decorative activity.
Check sound synchronization, intelligibility, clipping and narration completeness.
Identify any unmet item explicitly instead of claiming blanket compliance.
After publication, compare available swipe-away, retention, watch-duration and engagement data at comparable ages.
